concepts.def: If f is continuous and f(a) · f(b) < 0, there is a root in (a, b). Useful to locate roots before refining.
Rearrange equation as x = g(x). Iterate xₙ₊₁ = g(xₙ) from start value. Converges if |g'(x)| < 1 near root.
xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f'(xₙ). Fast convergence to root if starting value near root and f'(x) ≠ 0.
Approximates ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx ≈ (h/2)[y₀ + 2(y₁ + ... + yₙ₋₁) + yₙ] with strip width h = (b − a)/n.
Overestimates if curve is concave down; underestimates if concave up. Error decreases as n increases.
Newton-Raphson typically converges quadratically; fixed-point iteration linearly. Some methods diverge.

Numerical Methods — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Numerical Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Numerical Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Using Newton-Raphson on f(x) = x² − 2 with x₀ = 1.5, what is x₁? (Give to 3 dp.)
The trapezium rule estimates which kind of quantity?

numericals.q: Use trapezium rule with 2 strips to estimate ∫₀² x² dx (h = 1).

free_texts.q: What method uses xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f'(xₙ)?
